items.summary: Santosh Davakhar, writer-director-producer of the Marathi film Gondhal (English title Sacred Obsession), is India’s official entry for Best International Feature Film at the Oscars. He self-financed the 1960s-set debut after producers offered lower budgets than expected, spending under Rs 4 crore with GST, and added more on US promotion. Originally released November 14, 2025, it underperformed due to an unknown cast; Davakhar attributes this to low-key marketing. The film will re-release November 13 and compete alongside Angh, with Oscar nominations declared January 17 and the ceremony March 14. Davakhar remains confident of a nomination.
items.title: India’s Oscar Entry Gondhal Bets on All-Risk Gamble

items.summary: Two days of hearings on a legal challenge to Australia's landmark social media ban for children begin at the country's highest court. A digital rights group will argue that the under-16s rule robs children of free communication, while platform Reddit joins the case separately. The government says it will not be intimidated by legal threats.
items.title: Australia's social media ban faces High Court challenge

items.summary: Air quality across Delhi and the National Capital Region fell into the very poor category, with the overall AQI breaching 300 and crossing 400 in areas such as Rohini and Bawana. In response, the Commission for Air Quality Management enforced GRAP Stage Two measures including higher parking charges, diesel generator curbs, mechanical sweeping, additional metro trips, and Gurugram's work-from-home rules; the Supreme Court permitted only green crackers on limited dates.
items.title: Delhi AQI Enters Very Poor Category, GRAP 2 Imposed Across NCR Ahead Of Diwali

items.summary: Delhi Police ACP Manasvi Vashishta has been suspended after leading a protest outside the police headquarters on Monday, where scores of officers gathered to seek a meeting with Police Commissioner Anurag Kumar. The move follows an indefinite lawyers' strike over alleged threats by the ACP and Shahdara station house officer Arun Kumar in the Lalit Bansal assault case. Vashishta demanded clearer procedures for such matters.
items.title: ACP Manasvi Vashishta Suspended After Leading Delhi Police Protest

items.summary: A survivor statement accessed in the King George's Medical University conversion case alleges sexual abuse and drugging against Dr Rameez, spanning 2012 to 2025. The victim claims she was brainwashed against her religion, impregnated in 2016 with a pressured abortion, and assaulted after confronting him about affairs in 2024. An Uttar Pradesh Special Task Force investigation found Dr Rameez and his family complicit, leading to arrest; the High Court rejected bail.
items.title: Survivor Statement Alleges Abuse in Lucknow KGMU Conversion Case

items.summary: Delhi's overall air quality reached a hazardous level of 451 at 8 am on Tuesday, according to the Central Pollution Control Board. Monitoring stations in Rohini (429), Punjabi Bagh (424) and Bawana (408) recorded severe levels, while other areas ranged from very poor to poor. The Commission for Air Quality Management invoked Stage-II of GRAP across the NCR on Monday, prompting Delhi Police to conduct a checking drive at Ghazipur border as vehicle entry restrictions took effect.
items.title: Delhi Air Quality Hits Hazardous Level Before Diwali

items.summary: The Supreme Court ruled that a marital dispute or harsh exchange of words cannot by itself justify terminating a pregnancy, directing the husband opposing his wife's plea to file an affidavit withdrawing allegations made against her. The bench emphasised there was no medical reason for termination and posted the matter for November 4. Earlier, the Bombay High Court dismissed the woman's plea under the Medical Termination of Pregnancy Act, though a medical board had recorded she was in a fragile psychological state. The husband denied circulating WhatsApp messages but withheld evidence to preserve the relationship.
items.title: Supreme Court Bars Abortion Over Marital Dispute

items.summary: The alleged sting operation targeting former Karnataka Chief Minister Siddaramaiah has moved beyond police inquiry into a political dispute, with pressure shifting onto current CM DK Shivakumar. Former CM Siddaramaiah met Congress General Secretary KC Venugopal for about 30 minutes and Rahul Gandhi for around 40-45 minutes in New Delhi to raise concerns over the probe, per sources close to him. KPCC chief BK Hariprasad described the operation as “ugly” and urged identification of the real mastermind. HD Kumaraswamy accused Congress leaders of plotting against Siddaramaiah while the BJP stayed away from endorsing allegations directly.
items.title: Congress leaders shift sting-op focus from Kumaraswamy to mastermind

items.summary: A widowed adoptive mother of a 14-year-old boy from Noida has approached the Delhi high court to hand over his custody, alleging aggressive and hypersexual behaviour that left her, her elderly mother and sister fearful. Adopted at six, he is now described as intellectually disabled; she sought institutional placement while offering to contribute toward costs. The case prompts experts on adoption challenges. Santosh Koulagi of the Janapada Seva Trust says returning adopted children happens frequently, estimating 10 unreported cases per publicised one, though he notes this is an estimate rather than official data. CARA reportedly shared figures in 2020 indicating around four to five per cent of children adopted between 2017 and 2019 were returned. Counsel Dr Aloma Lobo says adoption requires effort from parents; Radha Nagesh advocates trauma-informed care and a special committee for difficult placements, while Sheila Ramaswamy stresses the child's welfare must remain central. The court has sought responses from CARA, the Child Welfare Committee and the boy himself.
items.title: Adoptive Mother Seeks Custody Handover for Teen in Delhi Court

items.summary: On Monday, Israeli forces injured two Palestinians near Bethlehem with bruises and demolished a memorial south of Nablus during raids across the occupied West Bank. Troops detained a young man west of Jenin, uprooted olive trees in Al-Lubban ash-Sharqiya, blocked roads, closed entrances in Hizma northeast of East Jerusalem, and removed a Palestinian flag from Iktaba. The Palestinian Wall and Settlement Resistance Commission documented 3,133 attacks by Israeli forces and occupiers in October, up 52.8% from September.
items.title: Israeli Raids Injure Palestinians, Demolish Memorial Across West Bank

items.summary: Fox's $22 billion acquisition of Roku is expected to move forward under a consent decree, according to people familiar with the deliberations. It remains unclear what terms would be involved, and officials said the Justice Department could still change course. The deal had drawn antitrust concerns that rivals feared Fox might favor its own content.
items.title: Fox-Roku Deal Poised to Clear DOJ Scrutiny Under Consent Decree

items.summary: More than 200 families served eviction notices in ward 65 of Tiruchy Corporation besieged Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay’s vehicle and convoy en route to Pudukkottai from the airport, holding placards and slogans demanding justice. The residents have lived over 100 years near a former tannery site allocated for labourers’ housing; the notice claimed private purchase of the land and ordered vacating within 10 days. Over 100 police personnel responded, spoke with protesters, and moved them aside to clear traffic, official sources said.
items.title: Tiruchy Families Block CM Vijay’s Convoy Over Eviction Notice

items.summary: A dispute over Vanavani Matriculation Higher Secondary School, inside IIT-Madras campus, has prompted retired staff member Inbamani to send a 13th petition appealing to Prime Minister Narendra Modi. The school, founded in 1963 with an initial 50 students and later over 2,600 pupils, now reports enrollment of 1,422 after intake curbs. Petitioners allege systematic winding down and Tamil marginalisation amid enforced Hindi study, seeking government intervention to preserve the institution.
items.title: Vanavani School Petitioners Urge Modi Over Closure Fears

items.summary: The Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration seized food stock worth Rs 9. 01 crore during a festive-season crackdown ahead of Diwali, including Patanjali cow ghee from M/s Divya Mahavitarak in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar. The FDA said 3. 53 lakh kg were confiscated for adulteration and hygiene violations, suspending 19 licences across Mumbai, Amravati and Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar. It also acted against edible oil from Avenue Supermarts Ltd and issued notices to Tata 1mg Healthcare, ACFO Pharma, Amazon and Flipkart over labelling concerns of Marine Collagen Powder. The drive ran Oct 28-31, seizing banned items worth Rs 79.
items.title: Maharashtra FDA Seizes Rs 9.01 Crore of Food in Diwali Crackdown

items.summary: Nathalia Gadelha Filgueiras, a 20-year-old co-pilot aboard the Learjet 60 that crashed in South Florida while flying from Austin to the Bahamas, was heard repeatedly calling 'Mayday' before impact. Recordings show she reported ice accumulation and temperatures of minus 47 degrees Celsius as the aircraft lost roughly 27,000 feet within a minute. Her mother said she had flown commercially for about nine months but lacked command authority.
items.title: Co-pilot's Final Mayday Call Before Florida Learjet Crash

items.summary: Air pollution in Delhi worsened ahead of Diwali, with the overall Air Quality Index reaching 451 at 8 am on Tuesday, indicating hazardous conditions. Data from the Central Pollution Control Board showed several stations recording severe levels—Rohini (429), Punjabi Bagh (424) and Bawana (408)—while others remained very poor. In response to a pollution spike, the Commission for Air Quality Management invoked Stage-II of GRAP across the National Capital Region on Monday, directing municipal corporations, traffic police and boards in Delhi, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh and Rajasthan to enforce sweeping, sprinkling, inspections and hotspot interventions.
items.title: Delhi Air Quality Hits Hazardous Levels as GRAP-II Restrictions Take Effect

items.summary: Control of Great Britain's 39m smart meters has passed to the non-profit Smart Energy Code Company (SECCo), replacing Capita-owned Smart DCC after more than a decade of rising costs and delays. The handover ends a licence granted in 2013, following an investigation into procurement contracts and a £200,000 payment into a consumer redress fund. A spokesperson said the network connects over 39.2m meters across 23m homes with 99.6% availability.
items.title: Non-profit startup takes over control of Britain's smart meter network

items.summary: A competitive Texas governor's race may shape one of the largest US data center markets as AI buildout opposition spreads internationally. Republican Gov. Greg Abbott revised earlier pro-data center policies, while his Democratic opponent pledged a stringent moratorium that could affect about 29% of net capacity additions planned nationally for 2028. Roughly 300-plus state and local moratoriums threaten the US buildout, as Australian and Indonesian projects face similar hurdles.
items.title: US Data Center Opposition Grows Globally
